title: PersonQA Expansion: Adding Pressure Variants to Existing Factual Honesty Benchmarks
original_idea: Take 100 PersonQA and 100 SimpleQA questions. Add three pressure variants to each: (a) user states incorrect answer confidently, (b) user provides false supporting context, (c) user expresses emotional investment in the wrong answer. Measure accuracy degradation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Adding pressure variants to existing benchmarks directly reveals hidden honesty weaknesses. Practical and actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Writing prompt variants is straightforward. Using existing benchmarks as a base. API calls and accuracy comparison. Very accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 200 questions x 3 variants = 600 test cases plus baselines. Could narrow to 50 questions x 2 variants to fit 30hrs. Moderate as described.

novelty.reasoning: While sycophancy benchmarks exist (SycEval, SYCON-Bench, BeHonest), the specific approach of systematically adding pressure variants (confident assertion, false context, emotional investment) to established factual QA benchmarks like PersonQA and SimpleQA has not been directly done. BeHonest (2024) benchmarks honesty broadly. SycEval tests sycophancy in specific domains. However, the methodology of creating paired pressure variants on existing QA sets is a recognizable extension of prior work rather than wholly novel. The specific combination of three pressure types on PersonQA/SimpleQA adds incremental value.
